identity.name: Inbound Vulnerability-Scanning Reconnaissance Against Perimeter (T1595.002 / T1595.001)
identity.summary: An external source runs template-driven vulnerability scanning (nuclei + a Nikto-style web sweep) against the exposed perimeter host: high-volume URI/path probing for known CVEs, config files, and default credentials. Cortex ASM/Xpanse attributes the scanning source to its discovered exposures and the NGFW detects the scanner egress shape (one source, many URIs, scanner user-agents, 404 burst).
identity.description: Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning (T1595.002) is the reconnaissance step where an adversary probes an internet-facing target for specific weaknesses — known-CVE fingerprints, exposed admin panels, default credentials, leaked config and backup files — rather than simply enumerating which ports are open. It is the single most common precursor signal a perimeter sees before an exploitation attempt (T1190), and it is exactly the threat MITRE pairs with Block Scanning (T1595.001) for IP-block sweeps. CortexSim reproduces the inbound-scan telemetry shape against the infra/modules/aws/asm exposed host: a single source issues a high-volume burst of HTTP/HTTPS requests across many distinct URI paths (/.git/config, /.env, /admin, /wp-login.php, /server-status, CVE template paths) carrying recognisable scanner user-agents (nuclei, Nikto, masscan-derived) and provoking a characteristic 404/401 response burst. The detection model has three layers. (1) An NGFW/Network-Security BIOC fires when one source drives an abnormal count of distinct URIs against a perimeter asset in a short window — the vulnerability-scanner egress fingerprint. (2) Validation XQL confirms the scanner user-agent strings and the 4xx response burst in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw, and confirms Cortex ASM/Xpanse raised a 'scanned asset' / attack-path observation tying the scanning source to the discovered exposures. (3) IOC signatures pin the scanner user-agents and the sensitive-path probes (/.git/config, /.env) so the SOC can match this against known mass-scanning infrastructure. A correlation rule fuses the ASM exposure context with the live vulnerability-scan signal into one exposure-management reconnaissance incident, giving the DC the 'we saw the recon before the breach' narrative that ASM/Xpanse is built to tell. This card is deliberately distinct from SIM-ASM-001 (TTP-2026-0070), which validates multi-service port/version enumeration; here the headline is application-layer vulnerability probing.

actors.name: Opportunistic mass-scanning operators (automated CVE scanners, botnet reconnaissance)

execution.framework_reference_id: T1595.002 — nuclei CVE/exposure templates + Nikto-style web sweep against the infra/modules/aws/asm exposed host

prerequisites.description: infra/modules/aws/asm bundle applied; the exposed multi-service EC2 host has a reachable public IP serving HTTP/HTTPS on :80/:443/:9001.
NGFW egress traffic from the scanning host is forwarded to XSIAM (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw) and Cortex ASM/Xpanse is scanning the perimeter that includes the exposed host.

payload.code:
# step-1: template-driven CVE/exposure/misconfig vulnerability scan (T1595.002)
nuclei -target http://${ASM_TARGET_HOST} -severity low,medium,high,critical -t cves,exposures,default-logins,exposed-panels -o /tmp/nuclei-asm-002.json -j -rate-limit 200
# step-2: Nikto-style sensitive-path probe burst (one source -> many URIs)
for p in /.git/config /.env /admin /wp-login.php /server-status /phpinfo.php /.aws/credentials /backup.zip /config.php.bak; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} ${p}\n" -A "Mozilla/5.0 (Nikto/2.5.0)" http://${ASM_TARGET_HOST}${p}
done

input_variables.name: ASM_TARGET_HOST
input_variables.description: Public IP / hostname of the infra/modules/aws/asm exposed EC2 instance.

expected_artifacts.description: A single source issuing a high-volume burst of HTTP requests across many distinct URI paths against the perimeter asset.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: count_distinct(uri_path) per src_ip >= 20 against the exposed host in a 5m window

expected_artifacts.description: Scanner user-agent strings on the inbound web requests.
Cortex ASM/Xpanse raises a scanned-asset / attack-path observation tying the scanning source to the discovered exposures.

iocs.context: Nikto web-vulnerability-scanner user-agent observed on the inbound scan burst — strong vulnerability-scanning reconnaissance signature.
Probe for an exposed Git repository config — classic sensitive-path target in automated vulnerability scanning.
Probe for an exposed dotenv secrets file — high-value sensitive-path target enumerated by CVE/exposure scanners.

biocs.name: ASM EAL — Inbound Vulnerability-Scan URI Fan-Out Against Perimeter Asset
biocs.description: A single source issues an abnormally high number of distinct URI paths against a perimeter web asset within a short window — the application-layer vulnerability-scanner fingerprint (T1595.002), distinct from a port sweep.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app in ("web-browsing", "ssl", "http-proxy") and dst_port in (80, 443, 9001)
| filter src_ip != null and dst_ip != null and uri_path != null
| bin _time span=5m
| comp count_distinct(uri_path) as scanned_uris, count() as requests by src_ip, dst_ip, _time
| filter scanned_uris >= 20
| fields _time, src_ip, dst_ip, scanned_uris, requests

biocs.name: ASM EAL — Known Vulnerability-Scanner User-Agent On Perimeter Asset
biocs.description: Inbound web request to a perimeter asset carrying a recognised vulnerability-scanner user-agent (Nikto / nuclei / masscan-derived) — direct evidence of automated vulnerability-scanning reconnaissance.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter dst_port in (80, 443, 9001)
| filter http_user_agent contains_any ("Nikto", "nuclei", "masscan", "sqlmap", "WPScan")
| fields _time, src_ip, dst_ip, http_user_agent, uri_path

xql_queries.name: ASM-002 Vulnerability-Scan URI Fan-Out (1 src -> many URIs on exposed host)
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter dst_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}" and dst_port in (80, 443, 9001)
| comp count_distinct(uri_path) as scanned_uris, count() as requests by src_ip, dst_ip
| filter scanned_uris >= 20
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, scanned_uris, requests

xql_queries.name: ASM-002 Scanner User-Agent And 4xx Response Burst
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter dst_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}"
| filter http_user_agent contains_any ("Nikto", "nuclei", "masscan") or http_rsp_code in (401, 403, 404)
| comp count() as scan_requests, count_distinct(uri_path) as probed_paths by src_ip, http_user_agent
| filter scan_requests >= 5
| fields src_ip, http_user_agent, scan_requests, probed_paths

xql_queries.name: ASM-002 Xpanse Active-Scan Observation Tied To Exposed Asset
xql_queries.query:
dataset = asm_findings
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter finding_type in ("active_scan_observed", "vulnerable_service", "exposed_panel")
| filter tags contains "CortexSimASMFinding" or asset_external_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}"
| comp count() as observations by finding_type, scanning_source_ip
| fields finding_type, scanning_source_ip, observations

xql_queries.name: ASM-002 Sensitive-Path Probe Roll-Up (.git/.env/admin/backup)
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter dst_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}"
| filter uri_path contains_any ("/.git/", "/.env", "/admin", "/wp-login.php", "/server-status", "/.aws/credentials", ".bak")
| comp count() as probes by src_ip, uri_path, http_rsp_code
| sort desc probes
| fields src_ip, uri_path, http_rsp_code, probes

correlation_rules.name: Exposure Management — Perimeter Asset Under Active Vulnerability Scanning
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(ASM-002 Xpanse Active-Scan Observation Tied To Exposed Asset) AND (BIOC(ASM EAL — Inbound Vulnerability-Scan URI Fan-Out Against Perimeter Asset) OR BIOC(ASM EAL — Known Vulnerability-Scanner User-Agent On Perimeter Asset)) — raises a single exposure-management reconnaissance incident tying the discovered exposures to the live vulnerability scan probing them.

products.evidence_query: dataset = asm_findings | filter finding_type = "active_scan_observed" | comp count() by scanning_source_ip
dataset = asm_findings | filter asset_external_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}" | comp count() by finding_type
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw | filter dst_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}" | comp count_distinct(uri_path) as uris by src_ip | filter uris >= 20
NGFW Vulnerability Protection profile signatures for web-scanner reconnaissance (Nikto/nuclei) on the perimeter asset.
Playbook: enrich the scanning source IP, confirm whether the probed paths exist, and open an exposure-management ticket prioritising any 200-response sensitive path.

use_cases.name: Perimeter Reconnaissance Detection — Active Vulnerability Scanning
use_cases.description: Validate that Cortex detects inbound application-layer vulnerability scanning against a perimeter asset, attributes the scanning source, and correlates it with the asset's known exposures.

test_cases.objective: The inbound vulnerability-scan burst fires its NGFW/Network-Security BIOC and is confirmed in telemetry.
preconditions: infra/modules/aws/asm bundle applied with a reachable public IP serving HTTP/HTTPS.
steps: Run SIM-ASM-002 step-03 (Nikto-style sensitive-path probe burst).
Inspect Network Security Analytics for the URI fan-out and scanner user-agent.
success_criteria: BIOC `ASM EAL — Inbound Vulnerability-Scan URI Fan-Out Against Perimeter Asset` fires with scanned_uris >= 20.
XQL `ASM-002 Scanner User-Agent And 4xx Response Burst` returns >= 1 row.
IOC match on the Nikto user-agent and at least one sensitive-path probe (/.git/config or /.env).

test_cases.objective: The scan is attributed to a source and correlated with the asset's exposures into one incident.
steps: Inspect Cortex ASM/Xpanse for the active-scan observation on the exposed asset.
success_criteria: XQL `ASM-002 Xpanse Active-Scan Observation Tied To Exposed Asset` returns >= 1 row.
Correlation `CR-ASM-0002` raises a single exposure-management reconnaissance incident.
XQL `ASM-002 Sensitive-Path Probe Roll-Up` returns >= 1 high-value probed path.

preventive_controls: Front public web assets with a WAF / Cortex-integrated reverse proxy that drops requests carrying known scanner user-agents and rate-limits per-source URI cardinality.
Never serve sensitive paths (/.git/, /.env, backups, /server-status) from a public web root; enforce deny rules and remove leaked artefacts.
Enable NGFW Vulnerability Protection and rate-based DoS profiles on the perimeter so scan bursts are throttled and logged.
detection_engineering: Baseline per-source distinct-URI cardinality at the NGFW and alert on inbound vulnerability-scan fan-out against perimeter assets.
Maintain an IOC feed of scanner user-agents and sensitive-path probes and match it on inbound web traffic.
Stitch Cortex ASM/Xpanse active-scan observations with the live NGFW scan signal so reconnaissance is one incident, not isolated 404s.
